system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Seller's updated SPA positions and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)
**Status:** Privileged – prepared for negotiation

## Headline view

The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Read against the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, the SPA positions do three things at once: (1) collapse the distinction between fundamental and general warranties so that even title and capacity are capped at 20% and time-barred at 18 months; (2) use general data-room disclosure plus a sweeping "Buyer knowledge" clause to neutralise the warranties on every known issue; and (3) push every live risk the Seller has itself identified (Bluefen consent, Riverlark debt, Ironquay IP, bonuses, the privacy incident, supplier costs) across the line to the Buyer at Completion. The Disclosure Letter is actually the more useful document – it candidly confirms that none of the key issues is resolved. We should use the Seller's own admissions against its SPA positions.

Issues are ranked by materiality below.

---

## A. Structural / liability regime

### 1. Fundamental and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits — **reject outright**
The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties "be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity", and that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".

- If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. A 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and an 18-month window on title is a transfer of the core deal risk to the Buyer. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- The title disclosure (para 10) compounds this: the Seller says title is evidenced only by the DD-012 share register and expressly notes the Buyer has not done its own verification. A share register is prima facie evidence only; it is not an ASIC search, not a review of the constitution/issue history, and does not reveal unregistered security interests over the shares (PPSR) or Riverlark's security package.

**Position:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency, shares fully paid and unencumbered) capped at 100% of price, with a limitation period of at least 6–7 years (ideally the statutory limitation period). Tax warranties and the tax indemnity: 7 years (ATO amendment periods). Specific indemnities: uncapped or separately capped, and not subject to de minimis/basket. Market in Australia for a deal this size strongly supports these carve-outs. Delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default and reverse it: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 2. "Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" (cll 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) — **reject**
This would subject the specific indemnities, the Riverlark/leakage protections, any price adjustment and claims for fraud/wilful misconduct to the 20% cap and 18-month bar. It would also attempt to exclude liability for fraudulent or misleading conduct, which is unenforceable in part (ACL s 18 cannot be contracted out of, and fraud carve-outs are universal) but creates argument.

**Position:** Express carve-outs from all limitations for fraud, wilful concealment, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, leakage, and claims under the covenants. Non-reliance clause acceptable only in the customary form (no reliance on representations *outside* the SPA and Disclosure Letter) and must not cut across the warranties or statutory remedies.

### 3. General cap, thresholds, time limit (cll 12.1–12.3)
- **Cap 20% / AUD 4.8m**: at the low end of market for a AUD 24m deal with this risk profile. Push for 30–50% (AUD 7.2–12m); the fall-back is 20% only if we get full carve-outs in items 1 and 2 plus a W&I-backed or escrow-backed structure.
- **De minimis AUD 25,000 and basket AUD 250,000 (excess only)**: an "excess only" (deductible) basket at ~1% of price is seller-friendly. Push for a tipping basket (first dollar recovery once exceeded) and reduce de minimis to ~AUD 10–15k, or at least allow aggregation of related claims. Make clear the thresholds do not apply to fundamental/tax/indemnity claims.
- **18 months for general warranties**: acceptable in principle only if (a) it runs from Completion and allows notification within 18 months with proceedings within a further 6–9 months, and (b) it does not apply to tax, fundamental or indemnity claims. Preference: 24 months to allow one full audit cycle plus a buffer.

### 4. Disclosure by general reference to data room and public registers (Sch 7 / DL paras 1.1–1.2) — **narrow substantially**
The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room and all "publicly searchable corporate records". Combined with cl 8.3 this means any warranty breach that is arguably traceable to any document, or any public register anywhere, is disclosed against.

**Position:**
- Disclosure must be "fair" – i.e. in sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed. General reference to a data room is only acceptable if the index is fixed and attached, the room was frozen at a stated time (the 22 Sept 2026 cut-off is at least a start), and the standard of fairness governs.
- Delete disclosure of "publicly searchable corporate records" generally. If retained, limit to specified ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia/court searches actually conducted and attached as at a stated date.
- Delete para 1.4's attempt to say nothing is admitted, or at least make clear that disclosure does not reduce the Seller's obligations under specific indemnities.
- **Importantly**: the Disclosure Letter is dated by reference to 22 September 2026. We are now in November 2026 and a number of matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident) are moving. We need a bring-down disclosure process with a strict rule that nothing disclosed between signing and Completion limits claims, with a termination right if new disclosure is material.

### 5. Buyer knowledge clause (cl 8.3) — **reject**
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." This is the most aggressive provision in the package:
- "Discoverable" is a constructive knowledge test — the Buyer loses claims for things it never actually knew but could theoretically have found.
- Imputing advisers' knowledge means a single line in a 300-page DD report defeats a warranty claim.
- It makes the warranties largely illusory and would negate the whole point of negotiating the Disclosure Letter.

**Position:** Delete. If the Seller insists on something, the only acceptable form is actual knowledge of a named small group of Buyer deal-team individuals, limited to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and expressly excluding the specific indemnities. Advisers' knowledge is never imputed.

---

## B. Specific commercial issues (all confirmed as unresolved by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter)

### 6. Bluefen change-of-control consent — **hard condition precedent, not "reasonable endeavours"**
Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. DD-002 has a change-of-control consent clause (11.2) with conditions (11.3). DL para 2 confirms no written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The Seller's position ("reasonable endeavours", consent "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent") is deficient:
- "Reasonable endeavours" is the lowest obligation. Should be "best endeavours" / "all reasonable endeavours" with Buyer involvement in the approach to Bluefen.
- The CP must require an **unconditional** written consent (or one whose conditions have been satisfied), in a form approved by the Buyer, with no adverse amendment to pricing, term or scope, and not expiring before Completion. "Delivery of written consent" alone is too thin if the consent is subject to 11.3 conditions that remain unsatisfied.
- The CP must be waivable by the Buyer only.
- Back-stop: if Bluefen consent is not obtained, either (a) no Completion, or (b) a price reduction / deferred consideration tied to Bluefen revenue retention for 12–24 months post-Completion. Given concentration, a retention-linked earn-out or escrow (~AUD 2–3m) is justifiable.
- Warranty that Bluefen has not given notice of termination/non-renewal and no dispute is on foot, plus a MAC termination right if Bluefen terminates between signing and Completion.

### 7. Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) — **repay and release at Completion, not after**
The deal is debt-free/cash-free. The Seller proposes the release is "provided following Completion". DL para 3 confirms the facility is not repaid, no discharge delivered, and there is a change-of-control clause (8.1). This means at Completion the Buyer acquires a company with AUD 3.2m of debt, security over its assets (and possibly over the shares), and a lender who can call default on change of control.

**Position:**
- Repayment out of the purchase price at Completion via the funds flow, with the Buyer paying Riverlark directly on the Seller's behalf (a deduction, not a post-Completion promise).
- Completion deliverables: executed deed of release/discharge of all security (and guarantees), signed PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to release within 5 business days backed by an escrow), release of any security over the shares, and written confirmation from Riverlark of the payout figure.
- Confirm whether any Harbourglass guarantee or cross-collateralisation exists and that no break costs are borne by the Company.
- Add leakage protection from the Locked Box date (if locked box) or a proper debt definition in the completion accounts that captures accrued interest, break fees and the Riverlark balance.

### 8. Closing bonuses AUD 420,000 (DD-005) — **Seller cost, must be in the funds flow**
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but has not itemised them. DL para 5 confirms they are triggered by Completion and continued employment, are not in the funds flow, and the Seller has not addressed payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs. If they are paid by the Company after Completion, the Buyer effectively pays them (plus ~15–20% on-costs: 12% SG at 2026 rates, NSW payroll tax ~5.45%, leave accruals).

**Position:**
- Treat as Transaction Costs / Debt in the price mechanics: deduct AUD 420,000 **plus** grossed-up employer on-costs and any employee-side tax withholding the Company must remit.
- Specific indemnity for any amount the Company pays in respect of these bonuses or any other transaction-related payments to employees, directors or advisers.
- Confirm the "continued employment" condition – if a bonus is forfeited because an employee leaves, the Buyer should not then be exposed to a claim; and if the condition is a retention device the Buyer wants, structure it so it is paid by the Company but funded by the Seller via escrow.
- Warranty that no other change-of-control, retention or transaction payments exist.

### 9. Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010) — **indemnity is inadequate; this is a title-to-IP issue**
Under cl 7.3 of the Ironquay SOW, title to the SOW3 Project Materials only passes on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment exists. The Seller's "indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment" misses the point: the issue is not AUD 180,000 of payables, it is that **the Company may not own the IP in whatever SOW3 built** – which for a data-analytics company could be core product code.

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion deliverable (or CP): Seller procures payment of the AUD 180,000 (as a Seller cost, deducted from the price if paid from Company cash), obtains Ironquay's receipt and a confirmatory deed of assignment of all SOW3 (and ideally all SOW1–3) Project Materials, with moral rights consents from the individual developers.
- If not deliverable pre-Completion: escrow (not less than AUD 180k plus a buffer) and a specific, uncapped indemnity for loss arising from any failure of title to the Ironquay materials, including the cost of re-procuring, licensing or re-developing them and any infringement claim by Ironquay.
- Expand the IP warranties: Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business; no third-party developer retains title or lien; no open-source contamination affecting the product. The Seller's statement that "IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime" is unacceptable while this issue is open.
- DD action: get bank evidence of payments to Ironquay; the Seller's DL para 4 expressly says DD-010 "is not independent bank verification".

### 10. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — **a specific indemnity, not "not expected to be material"**
A download link with ~1,240 personal records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) was sent to an unintended external address. The investigation is "preliminary". Risks:
- Notifiable Data Breach assessment under the Privacy Act 1988: if the data is likely to result in serious harm, OAIC and individual notification is mandatory; assessment must be done within 30 days. Given the mandatory assessment timeline and the Seller's own dating (22 Sept 2026), the assessment window has almost certainly expired by now – we need to know whether it was completed.
- Post-2024 Privacy Act reforms (statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy from June 2025; tiered civil penalties; OAIC infringement notices) materially increase exposure.
- Business-email data may be customer data (Bluefen?) – contractual notification obligations and reputational risk with the key customer.

**Position:**
- CP or pre-Completion covenant: complete the investigation and NDB assessment, deliver a written report to the Buyer, make any required notifications before Completion.
- Specific indemnity (uncapped, not subject to basket/de minimis, 6-year period) for all loss arising from the incident: regulatory penalties, notification costs, remediation, customer claims, third-party claims.
- Warranties on privacy/data compliance and no other incidents.
- Delete the Seller's cl 4.6 / Sch 6 characterisation as "not material" – that is a conclusion, not a disclosure, and DL para 6 itself declines to characterise the incident.

### 11. Supplier renewals AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011) — **verify before accepting "ordinary course"**
Three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The Seller says "ordinary-course operating costs"; its own DL para 8 says the disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that the documents must be read together for timing/scope.

**Position:** Request the contracts and the timing; if the renewals fall before Completion they should be priced into working capital / accrued as liabilities; if they are commitments created in contemplation of the sale (or outside normal cycle), treat as leakage. Add an ordinary-course / no-unusual-commitment warranty and a pre-Completion conduct covenant requiring Buyer consent for commitments above a threshold (say AUD 50k).

### 12. Mossvale (DD-009) and office lease (DD-007)
- **Mossvale**: the restriction is on *assignment*. A share sale is not an assignment, so on its face no consent is needed — but confirm the clause does not have a change-of-control limb, an "assignment includes change in control" definition, or a termination-for-convenience right Mossvale could use. Get a warranty that no Material Contract contains a change-of-control right other than those listed.
- **Office lease**: DL para 7 says notification, not consent. Confirm the clause; make notification a Seller pre-Completion covenant with evidence delivered at Completion. Check that the lease is not in the Seller's or a related entity's name.

### 13. Tax — **do not accept "settled under the general regime"**
No tax indemnity is mentioned. Standard for an Australian share acquisition: a separate tax indemnity covering all pre-Completion tax (uncapped or capped at price, 7-year period), plus tax warranties (lodgment, R&D tax incentive claims if any, payroll tax grouping, employee classification/PAYG/SG compliance – directly relevant to the bonuses). Confirm GST treatment of the share sale (input-taxed, no GST) and stamp duty (NSW has no duty on share transfers unless landholder duty applies – confirm Paperbark holds no NSW land interests ≥ AUD 2m).

---

## C. Process and verification points

- **Title verification**: run ASIC company and historical extracts, PPSR search against the Company and the shares, review the constitution and share issue history, and check for any options/convertibles. Do not accept DD-012 alone (the Seller itself says we haven't verified).
- **Data room cut-off**: freeze the index as at 22 Sept 2026 and attach it to the Disclosure Letter. Anything added later is not disclosed.
- **Bring-down**: warranties repeated at Completion; no "disclosure against repetition" except with a Buyer termination right.
- **Security for claims**: given the number of open items, propose a retention/escrow (suggest AUD 2.4–3.6m, i.e. 10–15%) for 18–24 months, or W&I insurance with the Seller funding the specific-risk exclusions.
- **Seller covenant strength**: Harbourglass is a "Ventures" entity; check it will hold assets post-sale. If not, require a parent guarantee or escrow.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties | Same 20% cap, 18 months | **Reject.** 100% of price; 6–7 years; tax 7 years |
| 2 | Limitations apply to all Claims | All claims, all limitations | **Reject.** Carve out fraud, fundamental, tax, indemnities, leakage |
| 3 | Cap / thresholds / time | 20%; AUD 25k/250k excess-only; 18m | 30–50%; tipping basket, lower de minimis; 24 months |
| 4 | General disclosure | Entire data room + all public records | Fair-disclosure standard; fixed index; delete public records |
| 5 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Actual + constructive + advisers | **Delete.** At most, actual knowledge of named individuals, fairly disclosed matters only |
| 6 | Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours; consent "on delivery" | CP for unconditional consent in Buyer-approved form; Buyer-only waiver; retention/earn-out if not obtained |
| 7 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Repay from price at Completion; discharge and PPSR releases as completion deliverables |
| 8 | Bonuses AUD 420k | "Matter for Seller", not in funds flow | Deduct from price with on-costs; specific indemnity; no-other-payments warranty |
| 9 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to AUD 180k | Pay + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; otherwise escrow + uncapped title-to-IP indemnity |
| 10 | Privacy incident | "Not expected to be material" | Complete NDB assessment pre-Completion; specific uncapped indemnity; privacy warranties |
| 11 | Sandbar renewals AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Verify; price into working capital or treat as leakage; conduct covenant |
| 12 | Mossvale / lease | No consent needed | Confirm clauses; warranty on change-of-control rights; notification as covenant |
| 13 | Tax | "Settled" | Separate tax indemnity + warranties; 7 years |
| 14 | Security | None | Escrow 10–15% for 18–24 months or W&I; parent guarantee |

**Negotiation framing:** The Seller's Disclosure Letter does the Buyer's work — it confirms on the record that every significant item is unresolved, undocumented or unverified. Our mark-up should lead with the point that a 20%-capped, 18-month, knowledge-qualified warranty package is only conceivable for a clean company; this is not one. Trade-off candidates we could offer in return for the fundamental carve-outs and the specific indemnities: accept the 18-month general period, accept a 25% (rather than higher) general cap, and accept a customary non-reliance clause.

Happy to turn this into a marked-up SPA and a response to the Disclosure Letter on request.
=== END ADVICE ===
